title: Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry Insights into the Assembly of Lanthanide-Containing Clusters
claim: A directed route to giant heterometallic hydroxide clusters can begin with structurally identified building blocks, prepare them separately, and assemble them using their connectivity as a design constraint.
explanation: The authors describe screening known structures for candidate nodes and linkers, examining their topology and synthetic conditions, verifying key units by ESI-MS, and combining building-block solutions to obtain large Ln–Ni frameworks.
scope: The reported family of giant 3d–4f lanthanide–nickel hydroxide clusters.
conditions: Separately generated compatible building blocks and control of inorganic linker length and node connectivity.
caveats: Predicted larger members of the topological family are design possibilities, not established products; the demonstrated route does not guarantee general applicability.
